title: Doubles: how they are shot and scored
summary: The kinds of doubles in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, how many cartridges you may fire at each target, and what happens when one shot breaks both.

body.html: A double is two targets shot on one call. Both disciplines have doubles on report and simultaneous doubles; only Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ also has the rafale. Some scoring rules differ. When both targets of a double are scored as lost, this is called zero-zero.
On report the second target leaves after your shot at the first, a simultaneous double leaves together, and the rafale (Sporting™ only) follows from the same trap.
body.heading: Watch how a double is thrown

body.html: First, singles. In both disciplines you may fire two cartridges at a single, so a first-barrel miss can still be saved with the second. A layout must leave time for two shots at each single.
In a double on report, your call releases the first target and your shot at it releases the second. In a simultaneous double, both targets leave together, and you may take them in either order.

html.sporting: Three kinds: on report, simultaneous (from one or two traps) and rafale. In a rafale, two targets leave the same trap on the same line, one after the other.
html.compak: Two kinds: on report and simultaneous. A simultaneous double comes from two different traps. There is no rafale.

body.html: In Sporting™ the second target of a double on report leaves 0 to 3 seconds after your shot at the first. In a rafale it follows as soon as the trap has reloaded. A double only uses targets already thrown as singles on that stand, so you have seen them fly.

html.sporting: Two cartridges for the whole double, and both may go at one target.
html.compak: One cartridge per target. Firing both at the first target is not allowed; doing it deliberately is scored zero-zero.

body.html: Both barrels firing together by accident is not a deliberate double shot: it is a gun fault, a double discharge. How it is scored is in Gun or cartridge malfunctions.

html.sporting: When your shot itself breaks both targets, both count: 'one' and 'one', in any kind of double. On report, the first target or its pieces may instead smash the second before your second shot. That is a No Bird: the double is repeated and the first result kept.
html.compak: On report: the first result stands, the second is a No Bird, and the double is shot again. Simultaneous: No Bird, shoot the double again; if it happens a third time, both targets are scored zero.

html.sporting: No shot at a simultaneous or rafale double without a valid reason: zero-zero. On report, a first target you do not fire at is zero, and the double is thrown again so that you can shoot the second (referees' quick guide).
html.compak: Refusing a simultaneous double: zero-zero. On report: a refused first target is zero; the double is thrown again so that you can shoot the second, and only the second is scored.

body.html: An irregular target is one that makes the referee call a No Bird, for example a target thrown broken, off its line or from the wrong trap (What counts as a hit, and what a No Bird is). In a double on report, an irregular first target means the whole double is thrown again. If it is the second target that is irregular, you shoot the double again and your result on the first is kept. The same applies if the first target or its pieces smash the second before your second shot. In a simultaneous double, and in Sporting™ a rafale, an irregular target means a repeat with nothing scored. One shot that breaks both targets is a different case: see above.
Watch the presentation and read the stand's menu, so you know which doubles are coming. Many coaches suggest choosing the order for a simultaneous double before you call.

notes.html: Compak® Sporting uses the same names as Sporting™ for doubles on report and simultaneous doubles (it has no rafale), but its doubles follow different rules. An interpreter who carries the Sporting™ rules over will give wrong answers.
Pass on a double's result as a pair, in the referee's order.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Report pair: the second comes on your shot.
phrases.meaning: Coach: the second target is released by the shot at the first.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: On the rafale, take either one first.
phrases.meaning: Coach: in a rafale double the order is free.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: Referee: both targets of the double are hits.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: Irregular target; the double is thrown again.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: One shot per bird on the pairs here.
phrases.meaning: Coach: in Compak® Sporting each target of a double gets only one cartridge.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Both with one shot. No Bird, shoot the double again.
phrases.meaning: Referee on a simultaneous double: nothing scored, repeat.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Choose your order on the show.
phrases.meaning: Coach: decide which simultaneous target to take first while watching the presentation.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: Referee: neither target of the double is scored.

key_points.html: On report, the second target is released by your shot at the first.
Sporting™: two cartridges per double, and both may go at one target; kinds are on report, simultaneous and rafale.
Compak® Sporting: one cartridge per target; deliberately firing both at one target is zero-zero.
Compak® Sporting has two kinds of double, on report and simultaneous; the rafale exists only in Sporting™.
One shot breaks both targets: Sporting™ scores one and one; Compak® Sporting has the double shot again.

did_you_know.html: In Compak® Sporting the double at each station starts with the last target of the previous station.

quiz.q: What releases the second target of a double on report?

options.text: The shot at the first target
A second call by the shooter

quiz.explain: The call releases the first target, and the shot at it releases the second.

quiz.q: In Compak® Sporting, may you fire both cartridges at the first target of a double?
quiz.explain: In Compak® Sporting it is one cartridge per target, and firing both at one target on purpose is scored zero-zero; in Sporting™ both may go at one target.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, one shot breaks both targets of a double. How is it scored?
quiz.explain: In Sporting™ both targets count; Compak® Sporting has different rules.
